ddx.step1_summary:
- Chief complaint: 2 days of lower abdominal (below umbilicus / suprapubic) aching with nausea and feeling hot/sweaty.
- Symptoms (onset/duration/severity/aggravating/alleviating): Symptoms began ~2–3 days ago, gradual onset, constant dull suprapubic ache causing nausea; feels hot/sweaty (subjective fever); no vomiting. Urinary frequency increased (no dysuria, no urgency, no foul smell). Had constipation about 1 week ago which has resolved; normal bowel movements since yesterday. Reports a little pink discoloration in urine or possibly spotting for the last couple of days and expects her period soon.
- Past medical history: No chronic medical problems reported.
- Medications / Allergies: No regular medications. Uses Implanon (etonogestrel) implant for contraception. Allergic to amoxicillin.
- Family / social history: Lives with boyfriend, sexually active with one partner. Brother has type 1 diabetes. Non-smoker.
- Vital signs / exam findings: None recorded in transcript; patient reports feeling hot/sweaty but denies light-headedness or fainting.
- Labs / imaging: None performed/not mentioned. Clinician advised face-to-face exam and pregnancy test.
- Other relevant negatives: No vaginal discharge, no severe localized unilateral pelvic pain, no vomiting, no syncope, no known fever measurement, no urinary pain or stinging.

V: Ovarian torsion: Torsion causes acute pelvic pain from vascular compromise of an adnexal structure — could present with lower abdominal pain and nausea. (Transcript: lower abdominal pain and nausea). Less likely given non-severe/dull and non‑sudden onset, but included because torsion is time-sensitive.
I: Urinary tract infection / acute cystitis: Suprapubic pain, increased urinary frequency and possible haematuria/’pink’ urine support cystitis. Feverish sensations and nausea can occur with more systemic involvement.

Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID): Lower abdominal pain, systemic features (feverish, nausea) and recent spotting/irregular bleeding plus sexual activity raise possibility; however patient denies vaginal discharge or multiple partners.
N: Ovarian cyst (rupture/hemorrhage) or adnexal mass: Can produce lower abdominal pain and acute/subacute nausea; may cause spotting. Less likely without acute severe focal pain or known mass but possible.
D: Constipation/functional bowel pain: She had constipation ~1 week ago which recently resolved; constipation can produce suprapubic discomfort and nausea.
Irritable bowel / transient gastroenteritis: Could explain nausea and abdominal ache, though diarrhoea/vomiting absent.
I2: Contraceptive implant–related bleeding: Implanon commonly causes irregular bleeding/spotting which could explain the pink urine/spotting; implant failure (pregnancy) is rare but possible and would be iatrogenic in the sense of contraception-related issues.
C: Congenital urinary tract anomaly (e.g., vesicoureteral reflux with recurrent UTIs): Unlikely new presentation but can predispose to UTIs causing suprapubic pain.
A: Allergic reaction / drug reaction: Unlikely — no new medications except implant placed previously; allergy to amoxicillin noted but not relevant to current symptoms.
T: Traumatic pelvic injury: No history of trauma reported; unlikely.
E: Pregnancy-related (including threatened miscarriage or ectopic pregnancy): Irregular bleeding/spotting, lower abdominal pain and nausea require pregnancy to be excluded. Ectopic pregnancy can present with abdominal pain and spotting and is potentially life‑threatening — clinician specifically recommended pregnancy testing.

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Pregnancy-related pathology (pregnancy with threatened miscarriage or ectopic pregnancy)
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Patient reports recent spotting/pink urine and lower abdominal pain with nausea; sexually active on Implanon (contraceptive failure is rare but possible). Clinician emphasized need to rule out pregnancy. Any pregnancy with pain/spotting must be excluded and ectopic pregnancy considered.
supporting_evidence: Spotting / pink-tinged urine reported over the last couple of days
Sexually active; clinician specifically advised pregnancy test
opposing_evidence: No frank heavy vaginal bleeding reported
No syncope, severe focal unilateral pain, or shoulder-tip pain described (classic ectopic red flags)

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Urinary tract infection (acute cystitis) with possible haematuria
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Increased urinary frequency, suprapubic aching, subjective feverish symptoms and pink-tinged urine are consistent with cystitis/hematuria. Nausea can be associated. Absence of dysuria/urgency makes classic cystitis less clear but does not exclude it.
opposing_evidence: No dysuria (painful or stinging urination) or urgency reported
No foul-smelling urine or other urinary symptoms noted
No urine dip / culture results available

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Lower abdominal pain, systemic symptoms (feeling hot/sweaty, nausea) and intermenstrual spotting can be features of PID. Sexual activity is present. However lack of vaginal discharge or multiple partners and relatively mild symptoms lower the probability.
opposing_evidence: No history of multiple sexual partners or recent new partner noted
Pain is described as a mild–moderate dull ache rather than severe pelvic pain

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Post-constipation / functional bowel pain (including IBS or transient constipation-related pain)
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: She reports constipation about 1 week ago which has since resolved; constipation can cause suprapubic discomfort and nausea. Normal bowel movement yesterday and lack of ongoing bowel symptoms make this plausible but may not account for the spotting and urinary frequency.
supporting_evidence: Suprapubic ache that could be bowel-related
opposing_evidence: Constipation has reportedly cleared and bowel movements are now normal
Does not explain pink urine / spotting or urinary frequency well
